answer: Like a jetty that only admits boats tied to a real berth, an agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each agent to stake a scarce, non-transferable credential earned through verifiable work before it can transact. New identities start at the dawn of their reputation with near-zero trust and tight quotas, so a single operator cannot wander in with a thousand cheap clones: each clone must separately pay the time and compute cost of proving useful, making mass fakery unprofitable while honest agents gradually earn higher limits.
